clue.text: Not entirely sure this fellow fitted for clubbing — not with it!

definitions.text: Not entirely sure this fellow fitted for clubbing — not with it!

indicators.note: to club something is to beat it about, so the letters gathered here are knocked into a new order
not entirely means the word sure is taken without its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its last letter goes
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS, Fellow of the Royal Society

indicators.note: not with tells you the word fitted loses the two letters named straight afterwards

parts.note: taken as written, before the two letters are removed
taken as written: the two letters to remove

explanation.surface: A doorman doubts that an unfashionable man is dressed right for a night at the disco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims sure to SUR, 'not with' it cuts fitted to FTED, and 'for clubbing' beats SUR, THIS, F and FTED into a new order. The whole clue also describes the man.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a pompous, stiffly formal man, just the sort who would look unfashionable and out of place in a nightclub.

clue.text: Employee who shouldn't be in the limelight?

definitions.text: Employee who shouldn't be in the limelight?

parts.words: Employee who shouldn't be in the limelight?
parts.note: limelight was the old theatre lamp that lit the performers; a backstage worker is paid to stay out of its beam, while the phrase usually just means public attention

explanation.definitionFit: A backstage theatre worker shifts scenery and props unseen, so is literally kept out of the lamps that light the actors.

clue.text: Not appropriate to drop female in one

indicators.note: to drop tells you the word for not appropriate lets one letter fall out

parts.note: something unfit for a purpose is not appropriate for it
F is the standard abbreviation for female, as on forms

explanation.surface: Leaving a woman out of a single group would be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in counting: a single thing or quantity, the number at the start of the count.

clue.text: Colt perhaps and mare gambolling under a tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, under puts the jumbled mare below the tree

parts.note: a fir is an evergreen conifer

indicators.note: gambolling is frisking about, so the letters of mare skip into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young male horse and a female one frolic beneath a conifer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gambolling' rearranges mare into EARM and 'under' sets it below FIR in this down entry. Colt looks like a young horse beside the mare; it is the American revolver maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Colt is a famous American make of revolver, one kind of gun.

clue.text: Not harming the environment in Scottish ridge shows good behaviour

indicators.note: in places the green prefix inside the word for a ridge

parts.note: drum is a Scots and Irish word for a long narrow ridge, as in drumlin
eco is short for ecological, describing things that do no harm to nature

explanation.surface: Green conduct on a Highland hillside is a sign of fine manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: propriety and seemly conduct in polite company.

clue.text: Entourage in hot French town working

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
Angers is a city on the Maine river in western France
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A celebrity's followers are busy in a sweltering spot in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the followers and dependants who trail around after an important person.

clue.text: Quick attack capturing pawn

indicators.note: capturing means the word for an attack takes the chess letter inside itself

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A swift chess assault wins a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both adjectives describe something happening at great speed.

clue.text: Roma clip spoilt broadcast

indicators.note: something spoilt is ruined and out of shape, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A damaged film extract from the Italian capital goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to announce something publicly and widely.

clue.text: Back packs fail to be more immediately available

indicators.note: to pack is to wrap up, so the word for back wraps round the word for fail

parts.note: the rear of something is its back
an engine that dies fails

explanation.surface: Rucksacks let hikers down by not keeping things close to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back packs' looks like one noun, rucksacks; split it, and Back is a word that 'packs', or wraps, the word for fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative adjective: something more prepared is closer to hand and can be used sooner.

clue.text: Star is able to get work

parts.note: can means is able to
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: A celebrity manages to find employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the second brightest in the night sky, in the southern constellation Carina.

clue.text: The German turned up in blue

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the German word is read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: das is one of the German words for the

explanation.surface: A German man makes an appearance dressed in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads DAS upwards in this down entry; 'The German' is the word 'the' in German, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: feeling blue is an informal way of saying unhappy or downcast.

clue.text: No room for French opera in city over there

indicators.note: no room means the abbreviation for room is absent from the opera's title

parts.note: Carmen is the opera by the French composer Bizet
RM is the abbreviation for room, as in property listings

explanation.surface: A theatre across the Channel is too full to stage a French opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Normandy port, with 'over there' pointing back to France, the country already named in the clue.

clue.text: Blonde vacuous type bores us agent

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the vacuous type goes inside the agent

parts.note: a fed is American slang for a federal agent, such as one from the FBI
an airhead is a silly, empty-headed person

explanation.surface: A flaxen-haired, empty-headed person wearies an American operative.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: describes someone with light, yellowish hair.

clue.text: Mix-up, for example remains of 19

definitions.meaning: a mix-up is a jumbling, here of the letters of a word into another word
the entry at 19 down has seven letters which, put in another order, spell the word remains, so remains is one instance of the device

explanation.definitionFit: A jumbling of a word's letters into another word, and remains is one such rearrangement of the entry at 19 down.

clue.text: Famous politician involved with lover's toe

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled or complicated, so the letters of the words after it are tangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: A well-known statesman gets entangled with his sweetheart's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Theodore and Franklin D. were both American presidents with this surname.

clue.text: Thought about lives being wasted

indicators.note: about means the word for thought goes round the word for lives

parts.note: mused means thought deeply or pondered
as a verb, lives means exists, or is

explanation.surface: Someone reflects sadly on squandered lifetimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' reads as a plural noun in the surface, but it is the verb: he lives, he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something squandered or put to poor use.

clue.text: Huge flans served up — that's the plan

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means both words are read from the bottom to the top as one run

parts.note: mega is informal for huge
flans are open pastry tarts

explanation.surface: Enormous pastries are dished up as part of the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reads MEGA TARTS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scheme or ruse devised to achieve an aim.

clue.text: Game plans on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio you only hear a word, so the word for plans is taken by its sound

parts.note: drafts are preliminary plans or outlines

explanation.surface: A wireless programme discusses match strategies.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the British name for the board pastime Americans call checkers.

clue.text: Ministry studies the latest stuff at home

parts.note: MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a British government department
to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn, so cons is studies

explanation.surface: A government department examines new household gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British phrase, short for modern conveniences: the up-to-date appliances and fittings of a house.

clue.text: Meeting house not available, right?

parts.note: a semi is the British word for a semi-detached house, one of a joined pair
NA is the abbreviation for not available, as in tables of data

explanation.surface: The chapel is booked up, and someone checks whether that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting house' reads as one thing, a place of worship; split it, and Meeting is the definition while house starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small gathering for discussion or teaching, as at a university.

clue.text: Cameron could be refreshed here?

indicators.note: refreshed means made new again, so the letters of the name before it could be given a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former British prime minister might recharge on holiday in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be refreshed' rearranges Cameron, and the whole clue is the definition: David Cameron was British prime minister, and this is a place where he might take a restful break.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balearic island and popular holiday spot, where a tired politician might go to recharge.

clue.text: Mum's blemish needs a cosmetic

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum; the 's is just the surface's possessive
a scar is a blemish left on the skin

explanation.surface: Mother covers a mark on her skin with make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: make-up brushed onto the eyelashes to darken them.

clue.text: What's furthest down flask in bag?

indicators.note: in places the flask inside the word for bag

parts.note: to net something is to bag or catch it, and a net is a mesh bag
a Thermos is a brand of vacuum flask for keeping drinks hot

explanation.surface: Someone asks which item is at the very bottom of the holdall and whether it is the vacuum bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a superlative meaning lowest of all, at the very bottom.

clue.text: Roll up for the essential part

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for a roll is read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll

explanation.surface: A showman's cry invites people to gather round for the most important bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads BUN from the bottom in this down entry; 'Roll up' looks like a fairground cry but splits into a bread roll and a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the crux or central point of a matter.

clue.text: Tax once levied on fruit? It helped to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A levy on orchard produce once did some good.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tenth of yearly produce paid to support the church, so a levy from the past.

clue.text: Endless platform for men

indicators.note: endless means the word for a platform loses its final letter

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A podium that goes on for ever is set up for the gents.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes an event attended only by males, such as a party before a wedding.

clue.text: Centres supposing that holding company held up

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means the assembled letters are read from the bottom to the top
holding means the word for supposing that has the company inside it

parts.note: if means supposing that

explanation.surface: Town hubs assume a parent firm has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding company' looks like one business term, but 'holding' is the container instruction; the result, ICOF, is then read from the bottom because 'held up' works vertically in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: the central points on which attention or light rays converge.

clue.text: One aquatic bird pecked another

parts.note: a bird that pecked you bit you with its beak
another refers back to aquatic bird: a tern is a slender seabird

explanation.surface: A water bird gives a fellow water bird a nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shy, booming relative of the heron that lives in reed beds and marshes.

clue.text: Great worry about very short time surrounded by …

indicators.note: about means the word for great worry goes round the very short time

parts.note: angst is deep anxiety or dread
a mo is informal British for a moment, as in half a mo

explanation.surface: Huge anxiety over a brief moment hemmed in by something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a preposition: in the middle of, with others on every side.

clue.text: … Narrow-minded attitude? It's Americans at fault

indicators.note: something at fault is wrong or defective, so the letters of the two words before it are put right in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the s of It's included

explanation.surface: People from the United States get the blame for a bigoted outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rigid, bigoted loyalty to one faction, especially a religious one.
